messages:
jess: FYI I saw weird failures in the ruby sampleapp during auth storms. tokens refresh OK but requests get retried immediately with no jitter and we hit rate limits downstream.

omar: that sounds like a retry/jitter parity issue vs go/js. which SDK version?

jess: ruby-sdk 0.9.1 from package. the retry backoff is deterministic (linear) whereas other SDKs use exponential with jitter.

chris: can you share a minimal log excerpt?

jess: sure: ```RETRY attempt=1 delay=0.5s; RETRY attempt=2 delay=1.0s; RETRY attempt=3 delay=1.5s``` other SDKs look like `0.6s, 1.8s, 0.9s` (randomized).

omar: ok that will cause thundering retries under bursty refreshes. We should align behavior. two quick fixes: 1) change ruby default to exp+full_jitter, 2) add a compatibility opt-out for strict linear backoff for customers who relied on it.

chris: add tests that compare the distribution of backoff samples across many runs so we don't regress. also add a short note in changelog about the policy change and why (rate-limit mitigation).

jess: I can open a tiny PR to switch to exp+jitter and add unit tests. will also add a sampleapp env var `REDWOOD_RETRY_POLICY` to mirror behavior locally.

ci-bot: build queued for branch `jess/retry-jitter` (job #4968).

omar: low-risk but important. let's keep PR minimal and backportable. if we get objections from enterprise customers about behavior change we can gate behind a minor flag for one release.

jess: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sdk/pull/601   (changed core backoff, added tests, CHANGELOG entry). requesting review from @omar @chris.

chris: reviewing now. good catch — thanks for the clear repro and the small patch.

jess: will also drop a note in the sampleapp README so folks running quickstart won't be surprised.
